craft.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for an ordinary Impeccable new-work request. It adds no behavior; natural build and redesign requests use the same flow.

init.description: Locally adapted: capture durable product truth in PRODUCT.md when explicitly requested or required by the selected project workflow. Reuse existing evidence and ask only about material gaps. Does not scaffold an app, configure Live, or make documentation a prerequisite to ordinary UI work.

document.description: Locally adapted: report or record the existing visual system from real code and permitted visual evidence when documentation is requested. Preserve the incumbent format; confirm a selected consumer's actual schema before claiming compatibility. Sidecars and other persistent helper state are separately scoped.

extract.description: Pull reusable patterns, components, and design tokens into the design system. Identifies repeated patterns and consolidates them. Use when you have drift across the codebase and want to bring things back to a consistent system.

live.description: Locally adapted: explicitly selected interactive browser variants for an existing local checkout, using a running app or supported static HTML target. Select elements, preview alternatives and accept or discard them. Launcher, injection, persistent state and service effects remain within current authority; ordinary UI work does not require Live.

generate.description: Locally adapted: agent-driven variants within an explicitly selected live-browser workflow. Resolve the named element and direction, then deliver the requested count for the user to cycle and accept. An ordinary request for UI alternatives does not by itself select helper startup, injection or persistent state.

adapt.description: Adapt designs to work across different screen sizes, devices, contexts, or platforms. Implements breakpoints, fluid layouts, and touch targets. Use when the user mentions responsive design, mobile layouts, breakpoints, viewport adaptation, or cross-device compatibility.

animate.description: Review a feature and enhance it with purposeful animations, micro-interactions, and motion effects that improve usability and delight. Use when the user mentions adding animation, transitions, micro-interactions, motion design, hover effects, or making the UI feel more alive.

audit.description: Run technical quality checks across accessibility, performance, theming, responsive design, and anti-patterns. Generates a scored report with P0-P3 severity ratings and actionable plan. Use when the user wants an accessibility check, performance audit, or technical quality review.

bolder.description: Amplify safe or boring designs to make them more visually interesting and stimulating. Increases impact while maintaining usability. Use when the user says the design looks bland, generic, too safe, lacks personality, or wants more visual impact and character.

clarify.description: Improve unclear UX copy, error messages, microcopy, labels, and instructions to make interfaces easier to understand. Use when the user mentions confusing text, unclear labels, bad error messages, hard-to-follow instructions, or wanting better UX writing.

colorize.description: Add strategic color to features that are too monochromatic or lack visual interest, making interfaces more engaging and expressive. Use when the user mentions the design looking gray, dull, lacking warmth, needing more color, or wanting a more vibrant or expressive palette.

critique.description: Locally adapted: return an evidence-scoped UX critique with applicable heuristic scores, concrete findings and strengths. Source or permitted rendered review can stand alone; detector execution, overlays, snapshots and persistent helper state are optional and subject to current authority.

delight.description: Add moments of joy, personality, and unexpected touches that make interfaces memorable and enjoyable to use. Elevates functional to delightful. Use when the user asks to add polish, personality, animations, micro-interactions, delight, or make an interface feel fun or memorable.

distill.description: Strip designs to their essence by removing unnecessary complexity. Great design is simple, powerful, and clean. Use when the user asks to simplify, declutter, reduce noise, remove elements, or make a UI cleaner and more focused.

harden.description: Make interfaces production-ready: error handling, i18n, text overflow, edge case management, and resilience under real-world data. Use when the user asks to harden, make production-ready, handle edge cases, add error states, or fix overflow and i18n issues.

onboard.description: Design onboarding flows, first-run experiences, and empty states that guide new users to value. Covers welcome screens, account setup, progressive disclosure, contextual tooltips, feature announcements, and activation moments. Use when the user mentions onboarding, first-time users, empty states, activation, getting started, new user flows, or the aha moment.

layout.description: Improve layout, spacing, and visual rhythm. Fixes monotonous grids, inconsistent spacing, and weak visual hierarchy. Use when the user mentions layout feeling off, spacing issues, visual hierarchy, crowded UI, alignment problems, or wanting better composition.

optimize.description: Diagnoses and fixes UI performance across loading speed, rendering, animations, images, and bundle size. Use when the user mentions slow, laggy, janky, performance, bundle size, load time, or wants a faster, smoother experience.

overdrive.description: Pushes interfaces past conventional limits with technically ambitious implementations — shaders, spring physics, scroll-driven reveals, 60fps animations. Use when the user wants to wow, impress, go all-out, or make something that feels extraordinary.

polish.description: Performs a final quality pass fixing alignment, spacing, consistency, and micro-detail issues before shipping. Use when the user mentions polish, finishing touches, pre-launch review, something looks off, or wants to go from good to great.

quieter.description: Tones down visually aggressive or overstimulating designs, reducing intensity while preserving quality. Use when the user mentions too bold, too loud, overwhelming, aggressive, garish, or wants a calmer, more refined aesthetic.

shape.description: Locally adapted: plan UX and UI before code and return the requested design brief. Reuse settled answers and project evidence, ask only about material unresolved choices, and stop before implementation or persistence unless separately authorized.

typeset.description: Improves typography by fixing font choices, hierarchy, sizing, weight, and readability so text feels intentional. Use when the user mentions fonts, type, readability, text hierarchy, sizing looks off, or wants more polished, intentional typography.
